interactions.summary: Jiang asks for a simple interpretation of Beatrice's cosmology, rejects a student's weight-based explanation as mistaken, and pushes the class to see why Dante would object to any model in which God arbitrarily loads souls differently.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang question with student answer and correction

interactions.summary: Jiang turns the discussion toward justice, saying Dante would reject Calvin-style assigned weights because such judgment would make God arbitrary rather than forgiving, and a student then asks how heaven and inferno can differ if God is not assigning the terms.

speaker_notes.note: The student's 'weights' explanation is clearly a trial interpretation offered for debate, not a settled lecture claim.

claims.claim: Jiang rejects the idea that God simply assigns fixed weights to souls, because Dante would experience that as unjust and as an intolerably judgmental picture of God.
Jiang explicitly contrasts this rejected model with Calvin, saying many Christians hold it but Dante as a Christian would still find it objectionable.

Jiang says multiple standards or forms of nature are part of the passage's logic, which means God assigns places and tendencies throughout creation without becoming a judge who arbitrarily condemns people.
Jiang says God cannot be understood as judgmental because the divine nature in this lecture is forgiving and generous, so the account of damnation must be explained some other way.

signature_moments.moment: Dante would be angry at a universe where God assigns heavy and light weights arbitrarily.
signature_moments.source_phrase: He'd be very angry at this idea
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It keeps the packet's moral energy: Jiang is not just parsing doctrine but judging which theological model Dante can live with.

signature_moments.moment: Never be judgmental, because that goes against the nature of God.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest ethical compression of Jiang's anti-Calvin turn in the packet and likely matters later for free-will and forgiveness themes.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A rejected explanatory model in which God preloads souls with heavier or lighter destinies, which Jiang treats as unjust and un-Dantean.
A mode Jiang opposes to the divine nature; if God is all-forgiving and generous, then arbitrary ranking or condemnation cannot be the right cosmology.

chronology_notes.note: This packet turns the abstract cosmic-order reading into an ethical-theological dispute about justice, setting up the next step where the class must explain heaven and inferno without falling back on divine arbitrariness.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's response to the 'many forms of natures' comment is compressed and slightly noisy, so later reuse should preserve the anti-judgment thrust without overfitting the exact mechanics of 'assigns everywhere.'
